Abstract does not report any comparisons between substance users and controls, so inclusion criterion I1 (empirical MRI study of GM differences between substance users and controls) is not met. The study does report striatal and cortical volumes (I2 met). No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are evident. Inclusion criterion I3 (any substance) is not demonstrated/applicable. Therefore exclude from the review.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent subjects to healthy controls using voxel-based morphometry to assess regional grey matter volume, meeting I1 and I2; substance is alcohol (I3). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group-other-than-substance, or review). Include for full-text review.

Abstract provides insufficient information to confirm it is an empirical MRI study comparing medication-overuse (a form of substance use) patients with an appropriate control group. Title implies gray-matter changes related to medication overuse in chronic migraine, but methods, imaging modality, substance type, and comparison groups are not reported. No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Include for full-text review to assess I1–I3.

EXCLUDED: Study examines Internet addiction (behavioral), not substance use. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E4 not applicable). Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses grey-matter structural measure: GMD via VBM). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a study of substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of a substance of abuse). Does not meet core requirement of substance-user sample.

Abstract reports cortical thickness MRI analyses in adolescent methamphetamine users (cortical thickness qualifies per I2; substance is methamphetamine, qualifies per I3). The abstract does not clearly state comparisons with healthy controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether GM differences vs controls were assessed.

Study examines social networking site (technology) addiction, not substance use; therefore it does not meet I1 (MRI studies comparing substance users vs controls) or I3 (studies of substances of abuse). It does meet I2 (uses voxel-based morphometry/GM volume). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met.

Excluded because this article is a meta-analysis (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (addresses grey-matter measures via voxel-based morphometry) and I3 (studies substances: cocaine and methamphetamine). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls).

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between heavy- and light-drinking adolescents (alcohol users vs controls). This meets I1 (MRI GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (alcohol is an eligible substance). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are indicated. Include for full-text review to confirm methodological details.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing cannabis users (n=141) and controls (n=120) reporting cortical surface measures (cortical thickness, surface area, gyrification). Matches inclusion criteria for GM structural measures and substance use comparisons; no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

E4: This is a voxelwise meta-analysis (systematic review/meta-analysis) and thus excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (addresses grey-matter VBM measures) and I3 (studies nicotine/cigarette smokers). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study assessing GM differences; it's a meta-analysis).

Exclusion E3: study compares gambling disorder (a psychiatric/behavioral addiction) patients to healthy controls rather than substance users, so it does not meet I1 (substance-user sample). Inclusion I2 is met (cortical thickness MRI measure). No other exclusion criteria apparent. I1 not demonstrated; I3 (any substance) not applicable/not demonstrated.

Study compares substance-naïve offspring with a family history of alcoholism versus controls, not substance users. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E4 not applicable). Inclusion IDs met: I2 (surface-based cortical thickness MRI). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (does not assess GM differences between substance users and controls), I3 not applicable because participants are substance-naïve. Therefore excluded from this substance-user vs control meta-analysis.

Abstract reports MRI findings in methcathinone (substance) abusers but does not clearly state comparison of grey-matter volume/density or specific GM structural measures versus controls. I3 (any substance) is met. I1 and I2 are not demonstrated from the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether GM volume/density comparisons with controls were performed and which structural measures were used.

Abstract reports an empirical structural neuroimaging study relating alcohol and cannabis use to gray matter (GM) volume and white matter integrity in adolescents and adults. It assesses GM volume measures and compares substance use to controls. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI study assessing grey-matter structural differences (cortical thickness and cortical volume) between amphetamine-type stimulant users and drug-naïve controls, matching the review objective. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are apparent from the abstract.

Abstract reports a methodological study applying cortical thickness to associations with drinking in 148 at-risk males. Inclusion criteria I2 (cortical thickness measure) and I3 (alcohol as substance) are met. I1 (GM volume differences between substance users and controls) is not demonstrated — no case-control comparison is reported. No exclusion criteria appear to be met. Abstract lacks sufficient information to determine if group comparisons were performed; full-text review needed.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses GM volume measures). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not a substance-user vs control MRI study), I3 (does not involve substance of abuse; studies online game addiction, a behavioral addiction).

Empirical VBM MRI study comparing abstinent heroin-dependent individuals to healthy controls, reporting gray matter density reductions (right DLPFC) and associations with duration of heroin use. Meets inclusion: I1 (MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I2 (uses GM density structural measure), I3 (substance = opioids/heroin). No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing abstinent alcoholics with controls using surface-based cortical thickness to map grey-matter loss; meets I1 (MRI GM comparison), I2 (cortical thickness allowed), and I3 (alcohol is an eligible substance). No exclusion criteria evident. Include for full-text review.

Study examines grey-matter surface-based measures (surface area) related to alcohol and cannabis initiation in adolescents, addressing the review objective. No exclusion criteria are identified. The abstract implies imaging (surface measures) but does not explicitly state MRI or control-group comparisons; full text needed to confirm methods and comparisons.

Study examines internet (behavioral) addiction rather than substance use; thus does not meet requirement to assess substance users vs controls. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cortical thickness is a gray-matter structural measure). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not a substance-use sample), I3 (not a study of any psychoactive substance). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met.

No exclusion criteria are met. Abstract reports resting-state fMRI with VBM gray-matter volume examined as a covariate, but does not clearly report case-control GM volume differences required by I1. Substance (betel quid) is within scope (I3). Insufficient information to confirm I1/I2, so include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an empirical VBM MRI study comparing opiate-dependent subjects to controls and reporting gray-matter density decreases. This meets inclusion criteria for MRI assessment of GM differences (I1), accepts GM density as a qualifying measure (I2), and the substance (opioids/opiate dependence) is within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey-matter (subcortical volume) between alcohol-dependent, polysubstance users and healthy controls. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) apparent from abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm details.

EXCLUDED because this article is a meta-analysis (E4). It analyzes GM differences in alcohol-use disorder, so it meets I2 (grey-matter structural measures) and I3 (substance = alcohol). It does not meet I1 (not an original empirical MRI study).

This empirical MRI study compares children with prenatal alcohol exposure (ARND) to controls and examines cortical thickness and surface area (surface-based grey-matter measures). It therefore meets I1 (empirical MRI comparison with controls), I2 (uses cortical thickness/SA as GM measures), and I3 (alcohol as the substance). No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Study compares gambling disorder (behavioral addiction) patients to controls, not substance users. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (psychiatric patient group as grouping variable). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (voxel-based morphometry assessing GM volume). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a substance-user sample), I3 (not about substance abuse).

Empirical English MRI study comparing grey matter volume between heroin users and controls (n=78 vs 79), so it meets I1 and I2. Substance is heroin (an opioid), meeting I3. No exclusion criteria are evident (no pharmacological manipulation, no brain lesion study, not a psychiatric patient-group comparison, not a review). Full text review recommended to extract specific regional data and methods.

The study compares baseline grey matter volumes between occasional stimulant users who escalated use versus those who maintained/reduced use — it does not compare substance users to non-user controls, so I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses GM volume measures), I3 (studies stimulants). No exclusion criteria are met (E1-E4 not applicable). Thus excluded for failing to meet I1 (no user vs control comparison).

Empirical MRI morphometric study in English comparing chronic alcohol users to nonalcoholic controls and reporting regional brain (grey-matter) volumes. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion focus, or patient-group other than substance use; not a review. Full-text needed to extract data and confirm details.

Title and abstract indicate an empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study of gray matter abnormalities in betel-quid-dependent patients compared to controls. Betel quid is an eligible substance. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric/neurological patient-group comparison, or review) are met based on the abstract.

Exclusion E3 met: study compares a psychiatric patient group (clinically depressed adolescents) to controls. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (voxel-based morphometry assessing GM volume). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not a substance-user vs control study), I3 (no substance of abuse studied).

Longitudinal empirical MRI morphometry comparing heavy-drinking adolescents to nondrinkers; assesses regional brain structural differences (fits grey-matter structural measures) and involves alcohol as the substance. No exclusion criteria met from abstract. Full text needed to confirm exact GM metric and details.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing alcohol-dependent individuals to age-matched healthy controls reporting gray matter volume differences related to decision-making. No exclusion criteria met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric grouping as primary variable, or review). Full-text review appropriate to extract coordinates and methods.

Study does not compare substance users to controls and so does not meet I1. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses voxel-based morphometry/GM structural measure). Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a substance-user vs control comparison), I3 (not about substances).

Excluded: animal experimental study with in utero alcohol administration (E1). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (cortical thickness measured) and I3 (alcohol as substance). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls; mouse embryonic histology rather than human MRI).

Excluded because population is behavioral (mobile phone) addiction, not substance users: inclusion I1 (MRI of substance users vs controls) is not met. Inclusion met: I2 (grey-matter structural measure assessed: GMV). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not substance use sample), I3 (not a study of any substance). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Abstract reports empirical MRI study using cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) comparing chronic cocaine users and controls; addresses GM structural differences between substance users (stimulant) and controls, meeting inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria met. Sufficient info for inclusion for full-text review to extract data on cortical thickness and group comparisons.

No exclusion criteria met. Study is a VBM investigation of time perspective in (presumably) healthy subjects, not a comparison of substance users vs controls; thus I1 (MRI study comparing substance users and controls) is not met. I2 (uses grey-matter volume via VBM) is met. I3 (study of substance use) is not met.

Empirical English MRI study comparing heroin-dependent individuals to healthy controls using cortical thickness (a valid surface-based GM measure). Substance = opioids (heroin). No exclusion criteria met from abstract (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group other than substance users, or review).

Empirical English MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing current smokers to never-smokers and reporting gray matter volume differences attributable to nicotine; meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Abstract reports cortical morphometry in substance-dependent individuals (a grey-matter structural measure) and is about substance dependence, but it does not explicitly state comparison with controls or explicitly name MRI; include for full-text to confirm I1.

Empirical English MRI study comparing adolescent substance users (SUD) to matched controls using T1 structural images and cortical thickness analyses. This satisfies I1 (MRI GM comparison), I2 (surface-based cortical thickness measure), and I3 (substance use sample). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, no lesion study, not a psychiatric/neurological patient-group comparison, not a review). Recommend full-text review to extract drug class details and methods.

No user-vs-control GM comparison reported: study reports VBM measures within 49 cocaine users only and relates GMV to TMS responses. Exclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (VBM GM volume measures), I3 (substance: cocaine). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (no comparison between substance users and controls).

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing structural (grey matter) measures in nicotine-dependent smokers vs controls using SUIT; fits the review objective and inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

Excluded: this is a review article (E4). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study), I2 (no original grey-matter structural measures reported), I3 (addresses substances but only in narrative review form, not as empirical data).

Empirical MRI study comparing cortical thickness and volume between marijuana users and controls in emerging adults. Meets I1 (MRI study assessing GM differences), I2 (surface-based measure: cortical thickness/volume), and I3 (cannabis as substance). No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Excluded because grouping variable is behavioral (online gaming addiction), not substance use — exclusion E3 applies. Inclusion I2 is satisfied (structural MRI cortical thickness). Inclusion I1 (empirical MRI of substance users vs controls) is not met; I3 (any substance) not met/not applicable.

Title/abstract report gray matter changes linked to methamphetamine (meets I2 and I3). Abstract does not explicitly state use of MRI methods or comparison between substance users and controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are evident from the abstract. Given insufficient detail to confirm all inclusion criteria, include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Empirical MRI study of cocaine-dependent individuals comparing brain gray matter to controls, reporting prefrontal GM reductions. This addresses structural GM differences in a substance-using sample (stimulant), meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3, and no exclusion criteria are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract examines prefrontal cortical thickness in betel-quid-dependent chewers (a grey-matter surface measure) and betel quid is an in-scope substance. However the abstract does not clearly state MRI methods or that users were compared to control subjects (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm group comparison and MRI details.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing grey-matter density between methamphetamine users and healthy controls (stimulant class). GM density is an eligible structural measure. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or patient-group diagnosis as primary grouping is reported. Meets inclusion criteria for full-text review.

Empirical MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent (recovering) participants to light-drinking controls using deformation-based morphometry to assess tissue (including grey matter) volume differences and longitudinal changes; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are met.

Abstract describes longitudinal prediction of future substance use in psychiatrically unwell youth using neural activity/structure, not a cross-sectional MRI comparison of substance users versus controls. Therefore I1 is not met; I2 and I3 are not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are clearly met.

Study examines alcohol misuse and mood disorders following traumatic brain injury (a neurological brain-lesion patient group) and does not report MRI grey-matter structural comparisons between substance users and controls. Exclusion met: E2 (brain lesion/TBI), E3 (neurological patient group). Inclusion met: I3 (study involves alcohol). Inclusion not met: I1 and I2 (no evidence of empirical MRI GM measures reported).

Abstract reports cortical gray matter loss in treatment-naïve alcohol-dependent individuals versus controls, addressing GM structural differences relevant to the review. The abstract does not explicitly state MRI modality, so full text is needed to confirm imaging methods and GM measure details.

Empirical MRI study comparing gray-matter volume between methamphetamine users and controls, meeting inclusion criteria for language and MRI GM volume measures (I1,I2) and substance type (I3). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison unrelated to substance use, or review). Include for full-text review to extract regional GM differences.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine users to non-drug controls and reports grey-matter structural measures (cortical volumes/thickness and nucleus accumbens volume). It addresses a substance of abuse (methamphetamine, a stimulant). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are met.
Study reports MRI structural differences (reduced dorsal prefrontal gray matter) in chronic ketamine users versus controls, satisfying inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Empirical English-language VBM MRI study comparing alcohol use disorder patients to controls and reporting grey-matter density reductions. Meets I1 (MRI GM differences vs controls), I2 (GM density measure), and I3 (alcohol). No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing grey matter volume between adolescent cannabis users and THC-naive controls, meeting I1 (MRI GM differences) and I2 (GM volume measure). Substance is cannabis, within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria appear met: no pharmacological manipulation, no lesion study, not a psychiatric patient-group comparison, and not a review. Include for full-text review.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing binge drinkers (substance users) to healthy controls and reporting grey-matter volumetric correlates. Meets inclusion criteria for GM volume measures and substance (alcohol). No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Study used task-based functional MRI of reward processing, not structural GM measures. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (contains alcohol-dependent group). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences vs controls) and I2 (no grey-matter structural measure such as GM volume/density/thickness reported).

Excluded because this is an integrative review (E4). No original empirical MRI comparison of substance users vs controls is reported: inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3 are not met or not demonstrated. The paper reviews structural/functional imaging in gambling disorder (a behavioral addiction), not empirical GM volume studies of substance-using groups vs controls.

The study reports MRI-based gray matter volume reductions in synthetic cannabinoid users versus healthy controls, meeting inclusion criteria I1 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (substance of abuse: synthetic cannabinoids). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met; include for full-text review.

E3: This study compares a neurological patient group (chronic migraine) to controls rather than substance users. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (MRI of substance users vs controls absent), I3 (not a substance-using sample), I2 (grey-matter measure of substance use not applicable).

Abstract reports an empirical structural MRI study comparing cortical gray matter volume in male adolescents with substance and conduct problems to controls, satisfying I1 and I2; substances are within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry reporting regional gray matter concentration reductions in MDMA (polydrug) users versus non-users. Matches inclusion criteria: MRI GM comparison (I1), GM concentration measure (I2), substance study (MDMA) within scope (I3). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are met in the abstract.

Study compares dependent vs non-dependent anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) users rather than substance users versus non-user controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (investigates a substance of abuse: AAS). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no clear MRI comparison of substance users vs non-user controls), I2 (abstract does not explicitly report grey-matter structural measures).

The study examines bone microarchitecture in hepatic cirrhosis, not brain MRI or grey-matter differences between substance users and controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an MRI grey-matter study), I2 (does not assess grey-matter structural measures), I3 (not a substance-use study). Therefore excluded from this review.

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing gray matter volume in substance-dependent individuals versus controls, finding reduced medial OFC GM. No exclusion criteria are met from the abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing FASD (prenatal alcohol exposure) participants to matched controls using cortical thickness (a valid grey-matter structural measure). Addresses alcohol-related GM structural differences and no exclusion criteria are met.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent men and healthy controls; reports regional GM volume decreases and correlations with executive performance. No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to extract regional GM alterations.

Large pooled MRI mega-analysis comparing gray matter volumes in substance-dependent individuals vs controls across multiple drug classes, matching the review objective. No indication of pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-grouping as primary variable, or being a review/meta-analysis. Therefore inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study does not compare substance users with controls: inclusion I1 not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness and subcortical GM volume measures). No exclusion criteria were met (none).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (study concerns amphetamine abuse, an in-scope substance). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an original empirical MRI study assessing GM differences; it is a narrative review), I2 (does not report original grey-matter measures). Therefore exclude for full-text review.

EXCLUDED because E4: this is a systematic literature review, not an original empirical MRI study. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (empirical English-language MRI study comparing substance users and controls) is not met; I2 (grey-matter structural measure) not applicable as primary data are not reported; I3 (study of substance users) is not met—focus is Internet Gaming Disorder (behavioral addiction), not substance use.

E4 met: this publication is a systematic review (not original empirical research). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study reporting original GM comparisons), I2 (does not present original grey-matter structural measures), I3 (although cannabis is the topic, primary empirical substance-user GM data are not reported in this review). Therefore exclude as a review article.

Empirical MRI study (English) reporting grey-matter volume (cingulum) differences associated with cannabis use (users vs non-users). Satisfies I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria clearly met from the abstract; grouping is cannabis use rather than psychiatric diagnosis. Include for full-text to verify sample/contrast details and extract data if eligible.

Excluded (E3): study compares adolescents with conduct disorder (a psychiatric patient group) vs controls — grouping is psychiatric diagnosis, not substance use. Inclusion: I2 met (reports cortical thickness/surface-based grey-matter measures). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 not met (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 not demonstrated (not about substance use).

Study compares alcohol‑naïve genetically vulnerable rats to controls rather than substance users versus controls; therefore I1 (comparison of substance users and controls) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (VBM grey-matter measure), I3 (substance = alcohol). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1–E4 not applicable).

Abstract reports empirical MRI study comparing cortical thickness/volume between substance users (methamphetamine-dependent) and controls, assessing grey-matter structural measures and interaction with HIV; meets inclusion criteria I1 and I2. No exclusion criteria met. Some uncertainty about primary focus on HIV but substance dependence is a grouping variable, so include for full-text review to confirm.

Abstract provides insufficient methodological detail to determine if it compares cannabis users vs controls (I1 not demonstrated). Title/abstract indicate MRI cortical thickness (thinner entorhinal cortex) and focus on cannabis liability, satisfying I2 and I3. No exclusion criteria are evident. Include for full-text review to confirm group comparison and measures.

Excluded: study compares schizophrenia patients to controls (exclusion E3). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls), I2 (no substance-related GM measures), I3 (not a substance-using sample).

Study compares adolescents with family history of AUD (FH+ vs FH-), not substance users versus controls; therefore it does not meet I1. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness, a permitted GM measure) and I3 (alcohol is the relevant substance). Inclusion not met: I1 (no MRI comparison of substance users and controls). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) appear to apply.

Empirical MRI study comparing grey matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid users and healthy controls, reporting reduced total and regional GM volume; meets I1 (MRI GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (substance of abuse). No exclusion criteria appear to apply (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review).

Title and abstract address cortical gray matter loss in methamphetamine users versus controls, suggesting relevant GM structural differences (I2) for a substance in scope (I3). The abstract does not explicitly confirm MRI methods or specific GM measure details (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met; full-text review needed to confirm methods and measures.

Exclusion E4 applies: this is a narrative/review article summarizing neuroimaging findings in medication-overuse headache, not an original empirical MRI study. Exclusion IDs met: E4. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no original empirical MRI study comparing substance users to controls), I2 (no primary report of its own grey-matter structural measures), I3 (unclear/other medication-overuse population not presented as substance-user cohort).

E4 met: Abstract describes an evaluation/review of female enrollment and methods across structural neuroimaging studies rather than reporting original empirical MRI comparisons. Inclusion criteria I1-I3 are not demonstrated: no primary empirical GM volume/thickness comparisons between substance users and controls are reported. Therefore exclude as a review/meta-research article.

Excluded per E3: study examines Internet Gaming Disorder (behavioral/psychiatric group), not substance users. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (reports VBM gray matter volume differences). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (study does not involve substances of abuse).

Meets inclusion criteria: empirical MRI study comparing adolescent marijuana (cannabis) users to non-using controls using cortical-surface based cortical thickness measures (a grey-matter structural measure). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are evident from the abstract.

Excluded (E3): the study compares pathological gambling (a psychiatric/behavioral addiction patient group) versus controls rather than substance users. Inclusion met: I2 (GM structural measure assessed). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not MRI of substance users vs controls), I3 (no substance of abuse studied). No other exclusion criteria apply.

Abstract reports structural MRI in opioid dependence examining compulsivity/impulsivity but does not state whether GM differences between substance users and controls were assessed or which grey-matter measure was used. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient information to confirm inclusion criteria from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Human MRI VBM study comparing regular cannabis users to occasional users; reports gray matter volume differences and correlations with use frequency and age of onset. No exclusion criteria met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion, patient-group comparison, or review). Satisfies inclusion criteria for GM structural MRI (I1, I2) and substance type within scope (I3).

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study of gray matter volume associated with heavy alcohol use in adolescents, meeting MRI and GM-measure criteria; no exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study comparing cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) between chronic cocaine users and healthy controls, which directly addresses GM structural differences in substance users. No exclusion criteria are met (not pharmacological, not lesion study, not a patient-group comparison for non-substance disorder, not a review). Full text is available for detailed data extraction.

This is a genome-wide DNA methylation study, not an MRI study assessing grey-matter structural differences between substance users and controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I2 (any grey-matter structural measure such as GM volume/density or cortical thickness). I3 (any substance) is not demonstrated with respect to neuroimaging outcomes.

Empirical T1-weighted MRI longitudinal study comparing cortical thickness between adolescents with cannabis use disorder and non-using controls (and across diagnostic groups). Uses a valid grey-matter structural measure (cortical thickness) and targets cannabis users vs controls. Not a pharmacological/lesion study or review. Presence of schizophrenia comorbidity is allowed because substance-use is a grouping variable and main effects of CUD are reported.

Study compares young adults exposed to harsh corporal punishment vs controls, not substance users. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses VBM to assess GM volume). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (does not compare substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of substance abuse).

Abstract discusses neural consequences of adolescent smoking but does not specify use of MRI, grey-matter structural measures, or comparison of substance users vs controls. No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient methodological detail in abstract to confirm inclusion criteria, so include for full-text review.

Empirical MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between long-term abstinent methamphetamine-dependent patients (stimulant) and healthy controls, satisfying inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

E3: The study compares psychiatric groups (patients with psychotic disorder, siblings, controls); the grouping variable is psychiatric diagnosis rather than substance-user vs controls. Inclusion met: I2 (GM volume measured), I3 (cannabis exposure assessed). Inclusion not met: I1 (no direct comparison of substance users and controls).

Abstract is insufficiently detailed to confirm MRI-based grey-matter comparisons between cocaine users and controls. Title suggests structural correlates in cocaine addiction, but no explicit mention of MRI, GM volume/density/thickness measures, or control comparisons. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine whether I1–I3 are satisfied.

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study (voxel-based morphometry) comparing gray matter volume between alcoholic patients and controls, matching the review objective for structural GM differences in substance users. No exclusion criteria are identified in the abstract (not a pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison unrelated to substance use, or a review). Full text review warranted to extract coordinates/measures.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none. (b) Inclusion IDs met: I3 (study involves opioids/polysubstance exposure). (c) Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 and I2 — abstract does not report empirical MRI data or any grey-matter structural measures (volume, density, thickness). Based on abstract alone, exclude for not meeting MRI/GM criteria.

Abstract does not report comparison between substance users and non-user controls, so I1 (users vs controls) is not demonstrated and the study cannot be included. The study does report grey matter density measures (I2) in cocaine users (I3). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met. Inclusion met: I2, I3. Inclusion not met: I1.

Empirical MRI study using surface-based morphometry (cortical thickness) comparing smokers and non-smokers within MDD and against healthy controls; nicotine is the substance of interest. Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract.

The study analyzes GM volume correlations within a sample of 176 social-to-heavy drinkers and does not compare substance users to a control group. Inclusion met: I2 (GM volume measured via VBM) and I3 (alcohol as the substance). Inclusion not met: I1 (no substance-users vs controls comparison). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) apply.

Study examines online game addiction (behavioral/non-substance addiction), not substance use. Inclusion met: I2 (VBM assessing grey-matter morphology). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I3 (involves a substance of abuse). No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) appear to apply.

Excluded because E1 is met: the study uses a pharmacological manipulation (adolescent intermittent ethanol administered intragastrically to rats). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness MRI/histology) and I3 (alcohol as the substance). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical human MRI study of substance users vs controls) is not demonstrated — this is an animal model. No other exclusions apply.

E3: The study compares cannabis-using vs non-using first-episode schizophrenia patients (psychiatric patient-group grouping), not substance users vs healthy/control participants. Inclusion met: I2 (GM volume measure) and I3 (substance = cannabis). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI study comparing substance users to controls) is not satisfied by the abstract.

Excluded because E3 applies: the study compares a psychiatric patient group (conduct disorder) to healthy controls rather than substance users. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (surface-based cortical measures such as cortical thickness). Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls).

Empirical English MRI study comparing hippocampal grey-matter volume between adolescents with alcohol use disorder and healthy controls, matching the review objective. No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or review; grouping variable is substance use).

Empirical MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent individuals (ALC) with healthy controls assessing regional gray matter volumes and relating them to cognitive/motor measures. Meets inclusion criteria for MRI grey-matter volume study of a substance (alcohol). No exclusion criteria apparent (not pharmacological, not lesion study, not review). Recommend full-text review to extract coordinates/measures.

No control group comparison is reported; the study examines family-history effects within alcoholic participants and reports total brain/ICV measures rather than grey-matter-specific regional GM metrics. Therefore inclusion criteria I1 and I2 are not met/not demonstrated. Inclusion I3 (alcohol as substance) is met. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) apply.

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study examining cortical thickness (a permitted grey-matter structural measure, I2) in relation to alcohol use (I3). The abstract does not clearly state a direct comparison between substance users and controls (I1 unclear). No exclusion criteria are met. Because group-comparison status is uncertain from the abstract, include for full-text review.

This is a non-empirical review/theoretical article summarizing prior neuroimaging findings rather than reporting original MRI data comparing substance users and controls. Exclusion criterion met: E4. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI study reported), I2 (no original grey-matter structural measures reported), I3 (no empirical substance-user sample described).

Abstract reports an empirical MRI study using VBM and SBM (cortical thickness) examining alcohol-related GM associations in a large sample; it addresses substance (alcohol) effects on GM. The abstract does not clearly state case-control group comparisons, so full-text review is needed to confirm I1 (user vs control group).

Volumetric MRI study in English assessing relationships between substance use (alcohol, cannabis, nicotine) and regional gray matter — meets I2 and I3. Abstract does not clearly report a direct comparison of substance users versus non-user controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are clearly met. Insufficient information to confirm I1; include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing hippocampal grey-matter volume between alcohol-dependent users and healthy controls; measures GM volume longitudinally; alcohol is an in-scope substance. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review) are met.

Prospective multisite study of adolescents initiating alcohol use reporting altered brain growth trajectories. No exclusion criteria are evident. However the abstract does not explicitly state MRI or grey-matter measures (I1/I2 unclear), so full-text review is needed to confirm eligibility.

Excluded because the comparison is a neurological patient group (medication-overuse headache) versus controls rather than a substance-use grouping (E3). Inclusion met: I1 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume) and I2 (GM structural measures used). Inclusion not demonstrated: I3 (study of substance users vs controls is not clearly the grouping variable).

Resting-state fMRI study of betel-quid-dependent individuals vs controls; gray matter volumes were calculated as a covariate but the abstract does not report between-group GM volume comparisons. The study meets I3 (substance of abuse included) but I1 (explicit GM volume group comparison) and I2 (clear structural GM measure reported as outcome) are not demonstrated in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) apply. Insufficient information to determine structural GM findings, so include for full-text review.

Empirical English MRI study comparing grey matter volume between heavy smokers and never-smokers using VBM; nicotine is within review scope and no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract coordinates and metrics.

Exclusion: No empirical MRI study presented. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing GM differences) not met; I2 and I3 not demonstrated. Abstract is a narrative review, not an original MRI comparison study, so exclude.

Excluded (E3): study compares antisocial personality disorder patients vs controls (psychiatric patient-group comparison), not substance users. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (MRI comparison of substance users vs controls) not met; I2 (GM structural measure in a substance-use context) not demonstrated. Therefore excluded from this review.

E3: Study compares narcolepsy patients (a neurological patient group) with controls, not substance users — thus excluded. Inclusion met: I2 (uses VBM, a grey-matter structural MRI measure). Inclusion not met / not demonstrated: I1 (does not assess substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of substance abuse).

Empirical English MRI study comparing methamphetamine-dependent adults to controls using a grey-matter structural measure (cortical thickness). Addresses GM differences between substance users and controls; no exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, no lesion study, not a psychiatric patient-group study, not a review). Include for full-text review to confirm details and extract regional GM results.

E3: the study compares schizophrenia patients (long-term antipsychotic treatment) vs controls, not substance users vs controls. It measures brain volumes (I2 satisfied) but does not assess substance use status (I1 not met) and is not about substances of abuse (I3 not met).

EXCLUDED: E4 applies (this is a narrative/systematic review of HIV neuroimaging, not an empirical study). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I2 (no grey-matter structural measures reported), I3 (not a substance-use sample). Study topic (HIV review) is outside the review objective.

MRI study uses cortical thickness (allowed GM measure) comparing children with fetal alcohol syndrome (heavy prenatal alcohol exposure) vs non-FAS and controls. Alcohol exposure is in scope. Abstract does not clearly show that subjects are 'substance users' themselves (exposure is prenatal), so eligibility is uncertain; include for full-text review to confirm.

Study examines Internet gaming disorder (behavioral addiction), not substance users. No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness and cortical volume grey-matter measures). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (MRI study of substance users vs controls) and I3 (study of a substance of abuse). Therefore excluded from substance-use GM meta-analysis.

Excluded due to E3: study examines cortical thickness in schizophrenia (psychiatric patient group) rather than comparing substance users with controls. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (uses cortical thickness as a grey-matter structural measure). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI comparison of substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of substance use).

Empirical MRI study comparing grey matter/cerebellar lobule volumes in individuals with Alcohol Use Disorder (n=24) versus matched controls, using structural volumetric measures. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are met. Abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry comparing grey matter between 20 alcohol-dependent patients and 20 controls; assesses GM volume/density and reports regional GM differences related to cognition and drinking; involves alcohol as the substance. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient group as primary grouping, or review) are met.

No exclusion criteria met. Inclusion I3 satisfied (study concerns alcohol exposure). Inclusion I1 and I2 not met: abstract reports fMRI functional activation during number processing, not structural MRI measures of grey matter volume, density, concentration, or cortical thickness. Therefore excluded.

Study examines Internet gaming (behavioral) addiction in adolescents, not substance users. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (GM volume measured). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not a comparison of substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of a substance of abuse).

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcoholic patients and healthy controls; reports GM volume deficits (a qualifying GM structural measure) and examines substance users (alcohol). No exclusion criteria are apparent (no pharmacological manipulation, brain lesion focus, patient-group other than substance use, or review).

Abstract reports MRI-assessed gray matter volume associations with habit-bias, indicating relevant structural measures (I2). However it does not clearly state a comparison of substance users (methamphetamine) versus controls or that MRI contrasts were performed between substance-user and control groups (I1 and I3 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are clearly met, so include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Empirical English MRI study comparing chronic alcoholics to matched controls reporting localized grey matter volume reductions. Meets I1 (MRI empirical study of GM differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (substance: alcohol). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are met in the abstract. Include for full-text review.

Excluded for E1 (pharmacological manipulation): study involves experimental cocaine administration to mice. Inclusion met: I1 (empirical MRI study comparing cocaine-exposed vs saline controls), I2 (grey-matter measures including cortical thickness), I3 (substance = cocaine). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: none.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing grey-matter structural measures (cortical thickness and hippocampal volumes) between methamphetamine users (with and without psychosis) and healthy controls. It meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3 and none of the exclusion criteria are met based on the abstract.

Exclusion: E4 (review/meta-analysis) and E3 (psychiatric patient group: IGD rather than substance users). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls), I2 (does not report grey-matter structural measures in substance users), I3 (not a study of substance abuse).

Voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing grey matter (and white matter) volumes in smokers vs controls (nicotine users). Meets inclusion criteria I1 (empirical English MRI GM volume comparison), I2 (GM volume measure via VBM), and I3 (nicotine substance). No exclusion criteria are met; full-text review appropriate.

Excluded due to E3: the study compares a psychiatric patient group (schizophrenia) vs controls. The study does use MRI regional brain volumes (I2 met). It does not examine substance users vs controls (I1 not met) and does not address substance use (I3 not met).

Excluded because E4 applies: the article is a meta-analysis/systematic review rather than an original empirical MRI study. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I2 (grey-matter measures are from aggregated studies, not original data in this paper), I3 (substance focus present but not as an empirical study).

Abstract reports an empirical longitudinal MRI study of alcohol effects on hippocampal volume in college students, assessing grey-matter volume (I2) and addressing alcohol (I3). The abstract does not clearly report a control group or between-group GM differences (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Insufficient detail on group comparisons -> include for full-text review.

The abstract reports an empirical English MRI study comparing daily cannabis users to nonusers, assessing gray-matter morphometry (voxel-based and surface-based measures) and controlling confounds. No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review).

Abstract reports quantification of regional gray matter volumes in substance-using and control groups but does not specify MRI as the imaging modality (likely pathological/post-mortem imaging). Insufficient information to confirm I1 (MRI), so include for full-text review to determine imaging method and eligibility.

Empirical structural MRI study comparing prenatal cocaine-exposed children vs non-exposed controls reporting grey-matter volume differences (cortical GM, thalamus, putamen). Cocaine is a stimulant within the review scope; no exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm eligibility and extract region-level data.

Participants are individuals with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (prenatal exposure), not substance-using adults/adolescents; grouping variable is a patient/disorder group rather than current substance use, so exclusion E3 applies. The study does use MRI cortical thickness (I2) and concerns alcohol exposure (I3), but it does not meet I1 (not comparing substance users vs controls).

Excluded (E3): study compares adults with ADHD (psychiatric patient group) to controls, not substance users, so it does not address substance-use related GM differences. Inclusion I2 met: uses voxel-based morphometry assessing grey-matter volume. Inclusion I1 and I3 not met/not demonstrated: no substance-user sample or substance comparison.

E4: Abstract appears to be a review of a decade of MRI studies (not an original empirical study). Inclusion met: I2 (discusses grey-matter measures) and I3 (alcohol as substance). Inclusion not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study comparing substance users vs controls).

Empirical MRI study comparing gray matter in treatment-naïve alcohol-dependent participants to nonalcoholic controls, assessing age-related GM shrinkage (a GM volume/structure outcome). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion, patient-group other than substance use, or review) are met in the abstract.

This study examines cortical thickness correlates of impulsiveness in healthy adults, not GM differences between substance users and controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (surface-based grey-matter measure: cortical thickness). Inclusion IDs not met or not demonstrated: I1 (MRI study comparing substance users vs controls not present), I3 (study of substance users not present). Therefore excluded from the review.

No comparison between substance users and non-user controls is reported; the study compares relapsers vs abstainers within an AUD sample. Exclusion IDs met: none (E1-E4 do not apply). Inclusion IDs met: I2 (cortical thickness/volume measures), I3 (alcohol as substance). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (no substance-user vs control GM comparison).

No substance-use grouping: study compares HIV+ vs seronegative controls, so it does not meet inclusion I1. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (GM volume measures). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not substance users), I3 (substance not addressed). Exclusion criteria met: none.

Empirical MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent individuals (n=20) to controls and reporting brain tissue (grey matter) volume decreases and associations with dependence/craving. Meets inclusion criteria I1 (empirical English MRI assessing GM volume differences), I2 (grey-matter structural measure: tissue volume), and I3 (substance: stimulant/cocaine). No exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing grey matter volume between active cocaine users and controls, reporting GM volume decreases. Meets inclusion criteria for MRI GM comparison, GM volume measure, and substance (cocaine). No exclusion criteria evident from abstract.

Meets inclusion criteria: empirical English MRI study comparing adolescents with alcohol use disorder to matched controls (I1); uses grey-matter measures (VBM, ROI, subcortical volumes) (I2); substance is alcohol (I3). No exclusion criteria met: not a pharmacological manipulation, not a brain lesion study, grouping is substance use not a psychiatric disorder, and not a review.

Abstract indicates study of opioid dependence and brain structural abnormalities but does not explicitly state MRI methods or grey-matter measures. No exclusion criteria are evident. Insufficient information to confirm I1/I2, so include for full-text review.

E1 met: study used IV cocaine infusion (a pharmacological manipulation). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (MRI cortical gray matter volume measures), I3 (substance = cocaine). Inclusion criterion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no comparison between substance users and controls reported in abstract).

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls; assesses cortical thickness (surface-based grey-matter measure) and reports GM differences for alcohol users. No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or psychiatric-group-as-primary-variable). Abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

Study examines structural correlates of resilience to traumatic stress in police officers, not grey-matter differences between substance users and controls. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (empirical MRI comparing substance users vs controls) not demonstrated; I2 (GM structural measures between substance users and controls) not demonstrated; I3 not applicable. No exclusion criteria clearly met. Excluded because it does not address the review objective (substance-user vs control GM differences).

The study examines cortical thickness and dopamine in healthy adults, not comparisons between substance users and controls. No exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion met: I2 (uses cortical thickness as a grey-matter measure). Inclusion not met: I1 (not an MRI study comparing substance users vs controls) and I3 (not a study of substance use). Therefore exclude from this substance-use GM meta-analysis.

Abstract reports an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume/structure between cannabis users, cigarette smokers, co-occurring users and controls; meets inclusion criteria I1-I3. No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are indicated in the abstract.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing frequent cannabis users to controls using subcortical grey matter volume measures; meets inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria. Full text recommended for extraction and meta-analysis.

E3: The study compares a neurological patient group (corticobasal syndrome/CBD) to controls rather than substance users. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of substance users vs controls) and I2 (GM measures reported are in a neurological disorder sample, not substance users).

MRI study comparing brain volumes between college-aged binge drinkers (alcohol users) and healthy controls; assesses grey-matter volumetric differences relevant to the review objective. Abstract does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Empirical English sMRI study comparing prenatally alcohol-exposed participants (FAS and PEA) to controls; reports regional brain volumes and contrasts white vs gray matter and regional gray-matter effects (e.g., parietal lobe), meeting inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to extract specific GM measures.

EXCLUDED because the study is not an MRI study (I1 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (assessed hippocampal gray-matter/volume measures) and I3 (alcohol as the substance). No exclusion criteria met. The abstract reports postmortem stereological measurements rather than in vivo MRI, so it fails the required MRI-based inclusion criterion (I1).

Empirical English MRI study comparing grey matter (orbitofrontal) between long-term cocaine users and controls; assesses structural GM differences. Meets I1 (empirical MRI, English), I2 (grey-matter structural measure), and I3 (substance = stimulant/cocaine). No exclusion criteria are evident in the abstract.
Title and abstract indicate an empirical neuroimaging study of gray matter in heroin (opioid) users vs controls, meeting inclusion criteria and with no exclusion criteria evident from the abstract.

Empirical MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing alcohol-dependent subjects and other groups, addressing structural grey-matter measures; meets I1 and I2. Presence of schizophrenia as an additional grouping variable does not trigger exclusion (comorbidity permitted) and does not prevent full-text review.

Empirical English-language MRI study using VBM to compare grey matter volume between heavy smokers (nicotine) and matched controls. Grey-matter structural measures reported (GM volume); substance of abuse is nicotine. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison, or review) are met.

Empirical English MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter density between cigarette smokers and matched never-smokers (nicotine use). Structural GM measure (density) is assessed; no pharmacological manipulations, brain lesions, or patient-group diagnoses reported. Include for full-text review.

Empirical VBM MRI study comparing gray matter volume between cocaine-dependent subjects and matched healthy controls; uses GM volume measures; cocaine is an included substance (stimulant). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, non-substance patient grouping, or review) are met. Include for full-text review.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between former heroin-dependent (opioid) subjects and controls. This directly assesses GM structural differences and meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group other than substance use, or review) are evident in the abstract.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing gray matter volume between individuals with cocaine use disorder and healthy controls, reporting reduced MCC GM volume in CUD and associations with ERP measures. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3; no exclusion criteria are met.

Empirical English MRI study comparing youth with heavy prenatal alcohol exposure to controls and reporting grey-matter structural measures (cortical volume, surface area, thickness, hippocampal volume). Matches review objective (structural GM differences related to a substance—alcohol). No exclusion criteria met (not pharmacological manipulation, not lesion study, not a patient-group comparison, not review).

No structural grey-matter MRI measures reported: this is an fMRI (functional activation) study, so I1 and I2 are not met. The study concerns prenatal alcohol exposure (I3 met). No exclusion criteria met.

Empirical study comparing brain cortical thickness in adolescents with substance use disorder versus controls, indicating MRI-based grey-matter (cortical thickness) measures. This meets I1 (empirical MRI comparison), I2 (cortical thickness as eligible GM measure), and I3 (substance users). No exclusion criteria (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group as primary grouping, or review) are evident. Include for full-text review.

Abstract describes longitudinal volumetric changes within alcohol-dependent patients related to interim drinking; it does not report comparisons between substance users and a control group. Inclusion I1 (GM differences between substance users and controls) is not demonstrated. Inclusion I2 (grey-matter structural measure via morphometry) and I3 (alcohol as substance) are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered.

The study compares adolescents with cannabis use disorder to adolescents without substance use, addressing substance-user vs control comparisons. Abstract does not explicitly state MRI or specific grey-matter measures, so inclusion criteria I1/I2 cannot be confirmed from the abstract. No exclusion criteria are met. Recommend full-text review to confirm MRI and GM measures.

E4 met: article is a review summarizing MRI evidence rather than original empirical research. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (addresses alcohol as the substance). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study assessing GM differences), I2 (does not report original grey-matter structural measures). Therefore excluded from this meta-analysis.

Empirical English MRI study comparing young adult smokers and nonsmokers; reports grey-matter structural measures (cortical thickness and subcortical volume) related to nicotine use. No exclusion criteria apparent (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review). Full text should be reviewed for details.

Empirical anatomical MRI study comparing cortical thickness between driving-while-impaired (alcohol) offenders and controls. Cortical thickness is an eligible grey-matter structural measure and alcohol is an in-scope substance. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison unrelated to substance use, or review) are met.

Exclusion E3: study compares persistent violent offenders with antisocial personality disorder (and substance dependence) to healthy controls — the grouping variable is a psychiatric/forensic patient group, not substance-user vs control. Inclusion met: I2 (MRI-based grey-matter measures: volumetry and VBM). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (MRI study assessing GM differences specifically between substance users and controls) and I3 (substance-users as the defined grouping variable/comparison).

Empirical MRI study comparing gray matter measures between heavy prenatal alcohol-exposed individuals and controls using surface-based and volumetric analyses. Fits inclusion: MRI assessment of GM differences (I1), includes surface-based GM measures (I2), and substance is alcohol (I3). No exclusion criteria met in abstract. Recommend full-text review to confirm details.

Meets inclusion criteria: I1 (empirical MRI study comparing synthetic cannabinoid users and controls), I2 (reports cortical thickness, surface area, and subcortical volumes — valid grey-matter structural measures), and I3 (synthetic cannabinoids are a substance of abuse). No exclusion criteria apparent in the abstract. Include for full-text review.

Title and abstract indicate a study of cerebellar subregional morphometry in individuals with alcoholism, implying grey-matter structural measures and an alcohol-using sample. However the abstract does not explicitly state MRI methods or clearly mention a control group, so full-text review is needed to confirm I1.

This is a narrative review article, not an empirical MRI study comparing grey matter between substance users and controls, so it meets exclusion criterion E4. No evidence in the abstract of original GM analyses (I1 not met), no specific grey-matter structural measures reported (I2 not met), and not an empirical substance-user study (I3 not demonstrated).

E3: Study compares schizophrenia patients vs controls (psychiatric patient group as grouping variable), not substance users. Inclusion: uses MRI-derived GM volume (I2 met). Not meeting I1 (not comparing substance users to controls) and I3 (not about substances).

Prospective MRI study comparing heavy marijuana+alcohol adolescent users to controls using cortical thickness (a surface-based GM measure). Meets inclusion criteria I1 (empirical MRI study of GM differences), I2 (cortical thickness measure), and I3 (substances — cannabis and alcohol). No exclusion criteria are met or suggested in abstract. Include for full-text review.

Title/abstract refer to early adolescent marijuana use and cortical architecture, implying a structural brain study, but the abstract lacks methodological detail to confirm it is an MRI study comparing grey-matter measures between substance users and controls or which GM metric was used. No exclusion criteria are evident. Include for full-text review to determine I1/I2 eligibility.

Excluded because E4: this is a review article (not an empirical study). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I2 (does not report specific grey-matter structural measures for substance users), I3 (not focused on substance-user samples).

No exclusion criteria met. Study is a postmortem neuropathological morphometric comparison, not an MRI study, so I1 (MRI studies) is not satisfied. It does report grey-matter volume measures (I2) and involves a substance of abuse (alcohol) within scope (I3). Excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I1 (MRI-based study).

E3: The study compares patients with psychogenic nonepileptic seizures (a psychiatric/neurological patient group) to controls, not substance users. Inclusion met: I2 (uses cortical thickness and VBM grey-matter measures). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no comparison of substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of substance use).

Empirical English-language MRI study examining associations between alcohol use and brain morphometry (subcortical volumes, cortical volume/thickness) in adolescents using co-twin control contrasts—provides comparisons of exposed vs non-exposed twins. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria are apparent from abstract.

Abstract is insufficient to determine whether this is an MRI study comparing substance users and healthy controls; title indicates grey/white matter changes in adolescent-onset schizophrenia with early cannabis use, suggesting a patient sample but unclear grouping (users vs controls or users vs non-users within patients). No exclusion criterion is clearly met. Include for full-text review to ascertain MRI methods and group comparisons.

Empirical English MRI study comparing grey matter between cocaine and heroin dependent patients and matched controls using 3D T1-weighted scans, reporting regional GM differences. Meets inclusion: I1 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I2 (grey-matter structural measures), I3 (substances include opioids and stimulants). No exclusion criteria met; include for full-text review.

Abstract reports prediction of relapse within a sample of alcohol-dependent patients (relapsers vs abstainers) using structural and functional MRI; it does not compare substance users to healthy controls. Thus I1 not met. Meets I2 (uses GM volume measures) and I3 (alcohol as substance). No exclusion criteria are met.

Study examines white matter microstructure in panic disorder patients with alcohol use; does not assess grey-matter structural measures required by I1/I2. Inclusion met: I3 (alcohol as substance). No exclusion criteria clearly met (E3 not clearly met). I1 and I2 not demonstrated (no grey matter measures).

Abstract is insufficient to determine whether this is an empirical MRI study measuring grey-matter structural differences between medication-overuse (substance-using) participants and controls. No clear information on MRI GM measures or comparison groups; no exclusion criteria evident. Include for full-text review to assess eligibility.

Abstract reports an MRI study of alcohol-dependent patients’ brain structure/atrophy relevant to substance use but does not specify case-control GM volume comparisons. Insufficient information to confirm I1; study substance (alcohol) is in scope (I3). Include for full-text review to determine whether GM structural comparisons with controls are reported.

Study compares non-drinking adults with a family history of alcohol dependence to controls, not substance users. Inclusion criterion I1 (empirical MRI comparing substance users vs controls) is not met. Inclusion met: I2 (GM-volume measure), I3 (substance = alcohol). No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded (E3): the study groups schizophrenia patients by aggression history/diagnosis rather than comparing substance users to controls. Inclusion met: I2 (GM volume measured). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (no substance-user vs control comparison), I3 (no substance was examined).

Longitudinal T1-weighted MRI comparing cortical thickness (a valid GM structural measure) between children prenatally exposed to alcohol (FASD) and controls. Matches inclusion criteria: empirical MRI study with surface-based GM measure and alcohol as the substance. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: prenatal exposure vs active ‘user’ status is ambiguous from abstract, so include for full-text review.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) between AUD patients and controls and high-risk relatives. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3 and no exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are evident from the abstract.

Empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing alcohol abusers (a substance-user group) and healthy controls, assessing regional grey matter volumes; meets I1, I2, and I3. No pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group-only design, or review indicated, so no exclusion criteria met.

E3 applies: the study’s primary grouping and research question center on a psychiatric patient group (schizophrenia vs controls) and schizophrenia-addiction comorbidity. Although it reports VBM grey-matter differences involving substance users (I1, I2, I3 satisfied), the psychiatric-grouping exclusion is met.
Empirical English structural MRI study comparing cannabis users and non-using controls; assesses grey-matter structural measures (gyrification, cortical thickness). No exclusion criteria met.

This study examines problematic Internet use (behavioral addiction), not substance users. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (GM structural measures: volumetry and VBM). Inclusion IDs not met / not demonstrated: I1 (study does not assess substance users vs controls), I3 (not a study of any substance). Therefore excluded as out-of-scope for a meta-analysis of substance-related GM alterations.

Exclusion E4 met: this is a meta-analysis/systematic review. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (examines GM volume measures via VBM), I3 (nicotine as substance). Inclusion not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study of participants vs controls). E1–E3 not applicable. High confidence because abstract explicitly describes a voxel-based meta-analysis of VBM studies.

Empirical MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent individuals to healthy controls and reporting gray matter volume differences (I1, I2). Substance is cocaine (stimulant), which is in scope (I3). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison unrelated to substance, or review) are apparent in the abstract. Include for full-text review.

Exclusion E4 met: this is a review article summarizing MRI findings in fetal alcohol spectrum disorders rather than an original empirical MRI study. Inclusion criteria met: none.
