Abstract is brief and does not state whether this is an empirical MRI study comparing substance users (alcoholics) to controls or which grey-matter measures were used. No exclusion criteria are clearly met from the abstract. Insufficient information to determine eligibility, so include for full-text review to confirm MRI and GM comparisons.

No clear substance-user vs control group comparison reported—study reports associations between lifetime smoking (pack-years) and striatal volumes within a community sample, so inclusion criterion I1 is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (GM volume measures) and I3 (nicotine as substance). No exclusion criteria met (none applied).

MRI study comparing grey matter volumes in individuals prenatally exposed to alcohol vs controls. Meets I2 (grey-matter structural measure) and I3 (substance = alcohol). Unclear if participants qualify as 'substance users' per I1 (they are exposure offspring, not users), so full-text needed to confirm relevance to review objective.

Study examines grey matter differences in internet gaming disorder (behavioral addiction), not substance-using populations. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (MRI assessment of GM volume). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI comparing substance users vs controls), I3 (participants are substance users).

Empirical MRI study comparing gray matter concentration between cocaine-dependent patients and controls; uses GM concentration (a valid grey-matter structural measure) and investigates a substance of abuse (stimulant). No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient grouping, or review) are evident from the abstract.

E4 met: article is a systematic review/meta-analysis, not an original empirical MRI study. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / not demonstrated: I1 (no empirical MRI comparison of substance users vs controls reported), I2 (no primary grey-matter structural measures presented), I3 not applicable (does not report primary data by substance). Exclusion applied: E4.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing grey matter volume between alcoholic patients and social drinker controls; reports GM volume differences and correlations with detoxifications. No exclusions (no pharmacological manipulation, lesions, or non-substance patient-group). Abstract provides sufficient evidence to include for full-text review.

Excluded because the abstract describes biochemical examination of cytoskeletal protein expression related to alcohol and ageing, not an MRI study of grey-matter structural differences. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (study involves alcohol). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume/differences), I2 (grey-matter structural measures such as GM volume/density/cortical thickness).

Abstract reports gray matter volume and morphological abnormalities in alcoholic Korsakoff's syndrome compared with controls, addressing alcohol-related structural brain changes. The abstract does not clearly state imaging modality details or full methods, so full-text review is needed to confirm MRI methods and measures.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between heroin-dependent (opioid) users and healthy controls. It assesses GM volume (meets I1 and I2) and involves an opioid-using sample (meets I3). No pharmacological manipulation, lesion focus, psychiatric-patient-group comparison, or review is indicated. No exclusion criteria met.

EXCLUDED because the abstract describes task-based fMRI activation to smoking cues (functional activation), not a structural MRI study comparing grey-matter volume/density between substance users and controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (nicotine substance). Inclusion IDs not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences) and I2 (structural grey-matter measures such as GM volume/density/thickness).

Not an MRI study of brain grey matter. Exclusion IDs: none. Inclusion met: I3 (study concerns a substance: nicotine/smoking). Inclusion not met: I1 (not an empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I2 (cortical thickness here refers to bone, not brain grey-matter cortical thickness).

Abstract reports analysis within adolescents with alcohol use disorders and does not mention a comparison to healthy or non-using controls, so it does not meet the requirement of assessing GM differences between substance users and controls.

Longitudinal MRI compares individuals with fetal alcohol spectrum disorders (prenatal alcohol exposure) to controls and reports reduced cortical gray matter volumes and volumetric analyses. This satisfies MRI assessment of GM differences (I1) and GM volumetric measures (I2); substance is alcohol (I3). No exclusion criteria apply. Although participants are not current substance 'users' but are prenatally exposed, inclusion criteria allow any substance exposure, so include for full-text review to confirm eligibility.

Excluded: the abstract is a narrative review, not an original empirical MRI study comparing substance users and controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI study), I2 (reports of grey-matter structural measures). The paper reviews evidence but does not present new GM comparison data.

Empirical structural MRI study comparing smokers (n=60) and nonsmokers with VBM-derived gray matter volumes and posthoc regressions; nicotine is within scope. No exclusion criteria met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion, patient-group comparison, or review). Abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

Empirical MRI study comparing regional gray matter volumes between adolescent frequent cannabis users and matched non-users; reports GM volume measures (amygdala-hippocampal complex, superior temporal gyrus, temporal lobes), meeting inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are met. Abstract provides sufficient information to include for full-text review.

Empirical English MRI study comparing cocaine-dependent subjects to non-drug-using controls using TBM and VBM to assess regional brain volumes (grey matter). Meets I1 (MRI study of GM volume differences), I2 (GM volume/density measures via VBM/TBM), I3 (substance = cocaine). No exclusion criteria met.

Voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing gray matter density between heavy marijuana users and non-users; meets I1 (empirical English MRI study comparing substance users vs controls), I2 (uses GM density measure), and I3 (substance = cannabis). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

E3 applies: study focuses on schizophrenia patients (psychiatric patient group) rather than comparing substance users vs controls. I3 met (cannabis exposure). I1 not demonstrated (no explicit GM MRI comparison reported) and I2 not met (abstract reports white-matter, not grey-matter measures).

Abstract reports MRI-assessed gray matter volume related to prenatal cocaine exposure in adolescents (meets I2 and I3). However, it is unclear from the abstract whether the study compares substance users vs controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are apparent. Include for full-text review to determine whether grouping matches substance-users vs controls.

Abstract indicates an MRI study of gray-matter volume in alcoholic subjects, satisfying I2 (GM volume measure) and I3 (alcohol is an eligible substance). The abstract does not explicitly report comparisons with a control group or between-group GM differences, so I1 (GM differences between substance users and controls) is not confirmed. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm presence of control comparisons and between-group analyses.

Excluded because the study used CT morphometric analysis rather than MRI. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (grey-matter structural measure via morphometric analysis), I3 (alcohol as substance). Inclusion IDs not met: I1 (not an MRI study assessing GM volume differences).

This is an empirical structural MRI study comparing children with prenatal alcohol exposure (substance = alcohol) to controls and reports subcortical gray-matter volume differences and brain-behavior relationships. It assesses GM volume measures relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing heroin-dependent individuals to healthy controls using automated morphometric assessment of grey matter volume. Meets I1 (English empirical MRI study of GM differences), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (opioid substance). No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group-for-other-diagnoses, or review). Include for full-text review.

Abstract describes a longitudinal voxel-based morphometry study of methamphetamine users (GM volume measures) but does not state whether comparisons to a healthy control group were made. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm presence of a user vs control comparison and extract data if present.

Excluded because E1 applies: this is an animal study with continuous cocaine infusion (pharmacological manipulation). Inclusion met: I3 (study involves a substance of abuse, cocaine). Inclusion not met or not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical human MRI study assessing grey-matter differences between substance users and controls), I2 (does not assess grey-matter structural measures; reports white-matter DTI/FA).

Single-case forensic neuroimaging/genetics report; no group comparison between substance users and controls. Inclusion met: I2 (GM structural measure via VBM). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (empirical MRI comparing substance users vs controls) and I3 (comparison of substances/users not shown). Exclusion criteria met: none (E1-4 not applicable).

Abstract mentions grey matter changes in medication-overuse headache, suggesting possible structural neuroimaging in a medication overuse group, but it does not explicitly state MRI methods or confirm that grouping is substance users vs controls. Unclear whether medication overuse qualifies as the substance-use group for this review. Insufficient information from abstract alone — include for full-text review.

Empirical MRI VBM study comparing grey matter volumes between alcohol-dependent users and matched healthy controls (meets I1 and I2). Alcohol is an in-scope substance (I3). rTMS is a non-pharmacological intervention and does not trigger exclusion E1. Abstract provides clear GMV group comparisons but full-text needed for extraction, so include for full-text review.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study assessing regional GM volume associated with later substance use; compares adolescents who developed substance use problems vs those who did not. Meets inclusion criteria I1, I2, I3. No exclusion criteria (E1–E4) are clearly met from the abstract. Full text needed to confirm details and whether comparison meets meta-analysis population requirements.

Empirical structural MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between older adult cannabis users and nonusers, matching inclusion criteria I1 (MRI GM volume comparison), I2 (GM volume measures), and I3 (substance = cannabis). No exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are evident from the abstract.

Empirical MRI study comparing DXM-dependent adolescents/young adults to healthy controls; reports cortical thickness and subcortical gray-matter volumes (valid GM structural measures). No exclusion criteria apparent from abstract.

Abstract reports prenatal exposure to maternal smoking affecting brain development in adolescents; uses MRI and focuses on orbitofrontal cortex and drug use during adolescence — compares substance-related outcomes. However abstract text does not explicitly state MRI GM volume/density measures comparing substance users vs controls; inclusion likely but not certain from abstract alone, so include for full-text review.

Human MRI study compares brain shape and gray matter density between heavy prenatal alcohol-exposed subjects and controls using structural MRI and surface-based analyses. Meets inclusion criteria I1 (empirical MRI GM comparison), I2 (GM density and surface-based measures), and I3 (substance: alcohol). No exclusion criteria evident in abstract.

EXCLUDED: The abstract does not compare substance users to controls (I1 not met). It examines offspring with familial risk for alcohol dependence and prenatal alcohol exposure and reports gray-matter volumetric differences (I2) and concerns alcohol (I3). No exclusion criteria are met.

Empirical MRI study comparing AUD subjects and controls, reporting cortical thickness and volume differences relevant to grey matter alterations in substance users; no exclusion criteria met. Suitable for full-text review and potential inclusion in meta-analysis.

No exclusion criteria met. This is an empirical MRI study of alcohol users vs controls, but the abstract does not explicitly report grey-matter volume/density/thickness measures (reports ventricles, white matter, CSF). Unclear if GM differences were assessed—include for full-text review to determine eligibility.

Empirical MRI study comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and controls; reports GM volume differences. No exclusion criteria met (no pharmacological manipulation, not a lesion study, not a review, and grouping is substance-use). Full-text review warranted to extract coordinates and methods.

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing cocaine-dependent patients to matched healthy controls, reporting gray-matter volume differences (striatal and other regions). No exclusion criteria appear met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison, or review).

E4 met: this study is a meta-analysis/systematic review. Inclusion criteria met: I2 (reports grey-matter structural measures, e.g., hippocampal and GM volumes) and I3 (studies alcohol/substance users). Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical English-language MRI study of primary data; it is a meta-analysis). No other exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because E1: study uses pharmacological manipulation (repeated amphetamine administration). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/demonstrated: I1 (not an empirical human MRI study comparing substance users vs controls), I2 (grey-matter measures reported from histology/serial coronal sections, not MRI-based GM measures), I3 (study is an animal model, not human substance-user vs control sample).

Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to assess (para)hippocampal grey-matter tissue composition in frequent cannabis users versus matched controls. This meets inclusion criteria for MRI GM structural measures; no exclusion criteria are evident in the abstract. Include for full-text review to extract regional GM effects (even though VBM found no differences).

Empirical English MRI study comparing chronic alcohol users to controls with quantified cortical gray matter volume differences and regional analysis (prefrontal/frontal). No exclusion criteria apply (not pharmacological manipulation, not lesion study, not a psychiatric/neurological patient-group comparison as the grouping is substance use, not a review).

Empirical English T1-weighted MRI study comparing gray matter tissue density between abstinent cocaine users and non-drug-using controls using voxel-based morphometry. This directly assesses GM structural differences for a substance (cocaine). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review.

Abstract reports an empirical neuroimaging (MRI) study comparing gray matter volume in male polysubstance users versus controls, assessing GM volume abnormalities across substances including alcohol, tobacco, cocaine and cannabis. This meets I1-I3 and no exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Excluded under E3: study compares PTSD (psychiatric patient group) vs controls, not substance users. It reports GM measures (hippocampal size and VBM) so meets I2. Does not meet I1 (not an MRI study of substance users vs controls) or I3 (no substance examined).

Abstract reports volumetric measures including gray matter in alcohol-dependent individuals during early abstinence but does not state a comparison with healthy controls (I1 unclear). Alcohol is within scope (I3) and GM measures are reported (I2). No exclusion criteria met. Include for full-text review to confirm presence of user-control comparisons.

Empirical English-language MRI study directly comparing grey matter volume between cocaine-dependent individuals (n=60) and healthy controls (n=60), reporting GM volume differences and associations with clinical measures. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison only, or review) are met.

Empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing frontal grey-matter volumes between young adults with early substance use/problems and controls; assesses GM volume and relates volumes to externalizing behaviors. No evidence of pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, or primary psychiatric/neurological patient-group comparison. Fits inclusion criteria but full text needed for details (exact substances, imaging methods).

Abstract does not clearly report MRI group comparisons of GM between substance users and controls (I1 not demonstrated). It does report gray-matter volume associations in healthy volunteers and includes substance-using groups (methamphetamine-dependent, ex-smokers), so I2 and I3 are met. No exclusion criteria are apparent. Full-text review needed to confirm whether GM differences between substance users and controls were assessed.

Abstract reports MRI/MR-spectroscopy assessment of gray matter volumes in the hippocampus during alcohol withdrawal (meets I2 and I3). It does not explicitly state comparison between substance users and controls, so I1 is not demonstrated. No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to determine if user vs control comparisons are reported.

E3 applies: grouping variable is Internet gaming disorder (a psychiatric/behavioral patient group), not substance use. Inclusion met: I2 (grey-matter volume via VBM). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 (participants are not substance users vs controls), I3 (study does not involve any substance of abuse).

Empirical MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (GM volumes) comparing detoxified alcohol-dependent men to healthy controls; addresses grey-matter structural differences relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria met.

Abstract reports an empirical brain morphometry study comparing polysubstance-dependent and alcohol-dependent treatment seekers to light-drinking controls, assessing neocortical morphometric (grey-matter) differences and associations with smoking and cognition. Substances (alcohol, stimulants, nicotine) are within scope. No exclusion criteria are met or evident. Full text review warranted to confirm MRI methods and exact grey-matter measures.

Exclusion E3 applies: grouping variable is a patient group (perinatally-acquired HIV) rather than substance use. Inclusion I2 is met (GM volume measured). Inclusion I1 is not met/not demonstrated: the study does not compare substance users vs controls (substance use assessed only within PHIV group, not in controls).

The study compares detoxified alcohol-dependent patients to matched controls and reports voxel-based morphometry (an MRI method assessing grey matter volume), thus addressing GM structural differences. No exclusion criteria are evident in abstract.

E1 met: study uses a pharmacological manipulation (SALLRSIPA peptide treatment). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (not an MRI study of human substance users), I2 (no MRI-based GM measures; uses gross brain weight/volume in mice), I3 (addresses alcohol but in an animal model, not substance-using humans).

Abstract reports empirical MRI assessment of grey matter volume (GMV) comparing heroin abusers and healthy controls (MRI sample n=154) and reports GMV differences and genotype-by-addiction interactions; meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are apparent (not a pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, diagnosis-group study, or review).

Empirical MRI study comparing nicotine-dependent individuals to controls using voxel-based morphometry (GM volume). Meets I1 (empirical English MRI study comparing substance users and controls), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (nicotine is an eligible substance). No exclusion criteria apparent (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison, or review). Abstract provides sufficient detail for inclusion in full-text review.

No evidence in abstract of a comparison between substance users and controls. Inclusion criteria I2 (grey-matter structural measure: brain volume) and I3 (substance = alcohol) are met. Inclusion criterion I1 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between substance users and controls) is not demonstrated; no control group or user-vs-control comparison described. No exclusion criteria clearly met.

Title/abstract report empirical study of subcortical volume and cortical thickness related to cannabis use in young adults (MRI structural measures). This addresses GM structural measures (cortical thickness, volumes) and involves a substance of abuse (cannabis). No exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

Empirical MRI voxel-based morphometry study comparing GM volumes between bipolar I patients with prior AUD, BD without AUD, and healthy controls; assesses GM volume (voxel-based) and targets alcohol use. No pharmacological manipulation, brain-lesion study, or systematic review. Substance-use (AUD) is a grouping variable despite comorbid bipolar diagnosis, so inclusion criteria are met.

Empirical MRI study in English comparing binge-drinking emerging adults to controls, measuring frontal cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) in relation to alcohol use. No evidence of pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, patient-group comparison, or review—meets inclusion criteria for full-text review.

Empirical English-language MRI study reporting grey matter volume differences associated with alcohol use (cotwin-control comparison). Reports reduced left lateral orbitofrontal cortex volume linked to drinking; no exclusion criteria apparent (not pharmacological, not lesion, not a patient-group comparison, not a review).

Prospective MRI study comparing gray matter volumes in treatment-engaged alcohol-dependent patients (after 1 month abstinence) versus healthy volunteers; uses GM volume measures and assesses relation to relapse. Meets inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria are evident from abstract.

Exclusion E3: study compares first-episode psychosis (schizophrenia) patients vs controls rather than substance users. Inclusion criteria not met: I1 (MRI study of substance users vs controls) is not demonstrated; I2/I3 not demonstrated. No other exclusions identified.

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing smokers and non-smokers on regional cortical thickness (a valid GM structural measure). Nicotine is a substance of abuse in scope. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, psychiatric patient-group comparison, or review) are met.

Abstract reports an empirical English-language MRI study comparing gray matter volume between chronic cocaine users and matched healthy controls, assessing frontostriatal GM structure and its relation to function/behavior. This satisfies inclusion criteria I1, I2 and I3, and no exclusion criteria (E1-E4) are indicated in the abstract.

Abstract does not report MRI or any grey-matter structural measures; therefore it does not meet I1 or I2. It does involve nicotine (I3 met). No exclusion criteria are clearly met based on the abstract.

Abstract reports MRI-assessed gray matter volume shrinkage in chronic alcohol users and evaluates SOD2 genotype, but does not clearly state comparisons between substance users and non-user controls (I1 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria are met. Include for full-text review to confirm presence of a user vs control GM comparison and extract measures.

Abstract reports MRI characterization of cortical gray matter in adolescents with cannabis use disorders, meeting I2 (grey-matter structural measure) and I3 (studies of a substance). It is unclear whether comparisons to healthy controls are reported (I1 not demonstrated) and no exclusion criteria are met from the abstract. Include for full-text review to confirm case-control comparisons and extract data if present.

Excluded: meets E1 (pharmacological manipulation—postnatal ethanol treatment in mice). E3 met: study compares psychiatric patient group (high-psychopathy patients) versus healthy controls. Inclusion: I2 met (voxel-based morphometry assessing grey-matter reductions). Empirical English MRI study using voxel-based morphometry comparing gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls, meeting I1–I3. No exclusion criteria are met (no pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, non-substance patient group, or review).

The study reports GMV correlations within a sample of social drinkers and risk factors, not GM volume differences between substance users and a control group. Inclusion I1 is not met. Empirical English MRI study comparing individuals with prenatal alcohol exposure (FASD) to healthy controls; reports grey-matter measures including regional brain volumes and cortical thickness, satisfying inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria from abstract are met.

Empirical MRI study comparing methamphetamine-dependent subjects and healthy controls using structural MRI cortical thickness measures (GM). Meets inclusion: assesses grey matter structural differences (cortical thickness), substance user group (methamphetamine). No exclusion criteria apparent.

Structural MRI (tensor-based morphometry) comparing children with prenatal alcohol exposure/FASD vs controls (meets I1 and I3). Abstract does not explicitly state grey-matter–specific measures (I2 not demonstrated). No exclusion criteria apparent. Include for full-text review to confirm GM-specific metrics and extract regional GM results if present.

This is a narrative review/survey, not an original empirical MRI study: exclusion E4 applies. Inclusion criteria met: none. The study is a functional MRI (BOLD) task study of MDMA users and does not report empirical grey-matter structural measures. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (substance of abuse: MDMA). Abstract reports an empirical voxel-based morphometry MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent patients to controls and reporting grey-matter atrophy, meeting inclusion criteria I1, I2, and I3. No exclusion criteria (pharmacological manipulation, lesion study, non-substance patient-group, or review) are indicated in the abstract.

Title and abstract indicate an empirical structural study reporting parietal gray matter volume loss in long-term abstinent alcoholic men compared to nonalcoholic controls, consistent with MRI GM volume comparisons. Satisfies I1 (MRI GM volume comparison), I2 (GM volume measure), and I3 (alcohol as substance). No exclusion criteria are apparent from the abstract.

(a) Exclusion IDs met: none (E1–E4 do not apply). (b) Inclusion IDs met: none. Abstract reports an empirical English-language MRI study comparing gray matter volumes between substance users (cocaine- and amphetamine-dependent) and matched controls, measuring GM volume and subcomponents—meeting inclusion criteria. Abstract reports a human neuroimaging investigation of brain volume recovery during abstinence across substances and discusses regional GM volume changes, relevant to the review. Empirical MRI study comparing active heavy drinkers with light-drinking controls using T1-weighted images and automated measures of gray matter volume; addresses alcohol-related GM differences relevant to the review. MRI voxel-based morphometry study examining grey matter volume and its relationship to alcohol use and impulsivity. Meets I2 (GM volume measure) and I3 (alcohol as substance). Abstract examines prenatal methamphetamine and tobacco exposure effects on brain morphology in children but does not specify use of MRI or explicit grey-matter structural measures. Empirical English-language MRI VBM study comparing cannabis-using patients to non-using controls (SCH+CAN vs SCH), assessing gray matter density; substance (cannabis) is within scope. Empirical English MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between substance users (heavy drinkers and smoking heavy drinkers) and non-smoking light-drinking controls. Empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volumes between adolescents with alcohol dependence and matched controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I3 (study involves cocaine-dependent subjects). E1 (pharmacological manipulation: within-subject heroin vs placebo). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (VBM GM density measure), I3 (study of opioid/heroin). Inclusion not met/not demonstrated: I1 — no comparison between substance users and controls (no control group reported).

Empirical English-language MRI study comparing grey matter volumes between college-age binge drinkers (alcohol users) and healthy controls, focusing on ventral striatum, hippocampus, and amygdala. Abstract reports empirical MRI analyses combining neural activation and local grey matter volumes in 40 alcohol-dependent patients versus 40 matched controls, meeting I1–I3. Abstract indicates focus on substance use disorders and structural brain alterations but does not clearly report MRI methods or whether substance users are compared to controls. Abstract does not clearly report an empirical MRI case-control comparison between substance users and non-user controls. Excluded because the study does not compare substance users with controls. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I2 (uses voxel-based morphometry rGMV measure). No evidence of a comparison between substance users and non-user controls in the abstract (I1 not demonstrated). Inclusion criteria met: I2 (grey-matter density measure). No exclusion criteria apply. Inclusion criteria not met/not demonstrated: I1 (case-control GM volume differences).

Empirical MRI study of cocaine-dependent individuals examining cerebral gray matter volumes (structural GM) and BOLD signals versus controls. Empirical English MRI study comparing poly-drug users and healthy controls; uses voxel-based morphometry and cortical thickness (an accepted grey-matter structural measure). No exclusion criteria are met in the abstract. Include for full-text review to extract regional GM differences.

Excluded because the abstract does not report comparisons of substance users versus non-user controls (I1 not met). Empirical English-language MRI study comparing cortical thickness (a grey-matter structural measure) between cocaine-dependent subjects and matched controls. Empirical MRI study (English) comparing alcohol-dependent participants (smokers and non-smokers) to non-smoking controls and reporting cortical thickness differences—cortical thickness is an eligible grey-matter structural measure. Abstract does not provide sufficient information to confirm it is an empirical MRI study measuring grey-matter structural differences between substance users and controls. fulltext_screening_results.reason: Although this is an empirical, English-language VBM study reporting whole-brain voxelwise GM volume differences with significant peak coordinates (meets I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, I9), it does NOT address the meta-analysis objective which is restricted to five pharmacological classes (alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis, stimulants). The current study examines betel quid (areca nut) users, a psychoactive but non-target substance class for this review. Therefore it is ineligible for inclusion despite satisfying the methodological inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none of E5–E7. Inclusion IDs met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion IDs not met: the study does not address the review’s target substance classes (alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis, stimulants).

This study reports empirical, English-language structural MRI VBM analyses comparing individuals with cocaine-use disorder (a stimulant class) to healthy controls. It uses whole-brain, voxelwise modulated GMV analyses (FSL-VBM, randomise) and reports significant between-group clusters (tables/figures/supplement) differentiating CUD from HC, satisfying the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain contrast. The paper provides grey-matter volume measures (modulated GMV), details of MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing/statistical software, and participant demographics. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not an atlas/parcellation-only analysis, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/supplement referenced). Thus the study qualifies for inclusion as a stimulant (cocaine) substance-use structural MRI comparison with controls.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing cannabis users and non-users and reports gray-matter measures (cortical thickness, gray matter density, regional volumes) (meets I4, I5). However, the paper’s analyses derive regional/parcel-based results using an atlas-based multi-atlas parcellation (Neuromorphometrics) and report per-region averages rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps with peak coordinates. No whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts yielding surviving significant clusters with reported (x,y,z) coordinates are provided (fails I6 and I7). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (atlas/parcellation-based results only). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between cocaine users (stimulant class) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (2×2 flexible factorial and planned whole-brain t-tests) that yielded significant clusters with reported coordinates (see Table 2 and figures) showing GMV differences (left IFG and bilateral vmPFC). Methods (4T scanner, SPM8, VBM8 preprocessing) and participant demographics are reported. Therefore it satisfies whole-brain voxelwise reporting with significant peak coordinates and provides the required GM measures for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study comparing alcohol-dependent (AD) patients and healthy controls, reporting voxelwise analyses and a between-group whole-brain contrast (voxel-wise two-sample t-test within a right-hemispheric mask) with significant clusters and peak coordinates (x=7.5, y=-51, z=1.5; cluster size reported) after cluster-level FWE correction. Grey-matter measures are modulated VBM (volume/density), MRI field strength (3.0T) and preprocessing/statistics (VBM8, SPM8, DARTEL) are reported, and participant demographics and substance-use measures are provided. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI (VBM) study comparing heavy cannabis users to controls and reporting voxelwise grey-matter results. It reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significant clusters and peak coordinates (e.g., medial temporal lobe/hippocampus-amygdala at x=-27,y=-10,z=-20 and superior temporal gyrus at x=-52,y=11,z=-15; pFWE<.05), satisfying the requirement for at least one significant whole-brain contrast with coordinates. Grey-matter measurements (GM volume/density) were used and preprocessing/MRI details (3T scanner, VBM8/SPM, DARTEL) and participant characteristics are reported. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volume between alcohol-dependent (AD) subjects and matched healthy controls (meets I4 and I5). The paper reports whole-brain univariate voxelwise analyses for the group contrast (controls > AD) with thresholded t-maps and refers to Supplementary Tables and figures for results (meets I6 and I8). The results describe significant clusters and regional effects (widespread GML) so qualifying significant foci are reported (meets I7). Participant demographics, MRI field strength, and preprocessing/software are reported (meets I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary tables are referenced but their absence in the provided file is acceptable per instructions, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-only as the sole between-group result, or non-empirical) are met. Minor uncertainty arises because coordinate tables are in supplementary materials not provided here, but the main text explicitly indicates voxelwise whole-brain results and supplementary coordinate tables, so inclusion is justified.

This is an empirical human structural MRI study comparing methamphetamine users and controls that reports whole-brain vertex-wise cortical thickness analyses and voxel-wise DTI results. Cortical thickness is an accepted grey-matter measure per I5. The paper describes vertex-wise and voxel-wise whole-brain contrasts and refers to significant clusters presented in Supplementary Figures/Tables (Supplementary Table 2, Supplementary Figure 2, Supplementary Figure 3, Supplementary Table 3, Supplementary Table 4), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain statistical maps and significant foci (I6–I8). Participant demographics and MRI acquisition/statistical details are reported (I9). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4–I9 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (e.g., it is not ROI-only or atlas-parcellation-only, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion); supplementary tables are referenced for coordinates.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between heavy adolescent alcohol users and matched light-drinking controls. The paper reports voxelwise analyses (VBM) and significant between-group clusters (ROI-restricted voxelwise analyses with small-volume correction) in ACC, orbitofrontal/frontopolar cortex, superior temporal gyrus and insula; results are presented in figures and a table with MNI coordinates. It therefore meets whole-brain voxelwise reporting requirements (I6) as the meta-analysis allows sub-volume voxelwise maps with reported coordinates. The study also meets I4 (empirical MRI), I5 (GM volume measure), I7 (significant foci with reported peaks), I8 (results reported in tables/figures), and I9 (participant demographics and MRI parameters reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

EXCLUDED because the study conducted whole-brain vertexwise analyses but reported null whole-brain results (no significant clusters surviving correction) and therefore does not meet inclusion criterion I7, which requires at least one significant whole-brain cluster with reported peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing substance users vs. controls), I5 (grey-matter surface measures: cortical thickness, surface area, gyrification are reported), I6 (whole-brain vertexwise statistical maps were performed), I9 (participant demographics, scanner field strength, preprocessing and software reported). This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing intravenous methcathinone (a stimulant) users with matched controls using whole-brain voxelwise VBM and vertexwise cortical-thickness analyses. The paper reports significant between-group grey-matter differences (striatal VBM reductions and multiple cortical-thinning clusters) and refers to figures/tables with MNI coordinates. Participant demographics, substance-use history, MRI field strength (3.0T), and preprocessing/statistical software (FSL, FreeSurfer) are described. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. It does not meet any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not atlas-parcellation-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The paper performs voxelwise VBM GLMs relating continuous alcohol (AUDIT) and cannabis (TLFB) measures to gray-matter volume, but does not present a whole-brain between-group contrast comparing substance users versus controls. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I4 (empirical MRI study assessing GM differences between substance users and controls) and I6 (must report a whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrast). The study does satisfy I5 (GM volume measured via VBM), I7 (reports significant voxelwise clusters with peak coordinates), I8 (results available in tables/figures), and I9 (reports age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing/statistical software). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete.

The manuscript is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing amphetamine-type stimulant users and controls and reports vertexwise whole-brain analyses of cortical thickness and cortical volume. Thus it satisfies I4 (empirical MRI GM study), I5 (GM measures including cortical thickness/volume), and I6 (whole-brain vertexwise statistical maps via Freesurfer QDEC). However, criterion I7 requires that at least one whole-brain contrast yields a significant cluster with reported peak coordinates (x,y,z). Although the text states significant clusters survived multiple-comparison correction, the provided full text does not include the peak coordinate tables/figures or explicit coordinate values (results are referenced as being in figures/tables/supplementary materials but these are not present). Because I7 cannot be verified from the supplied content and the coordinate information appears omitted, I cannot confirm the primary requirement for coordinate-based meta-analysis. Therefore I exclude this record due to incomplete reporting of required coordinate data in the supplied full text (fulltext_incomplete=true).

Exclusion decision because the paper does not report peak coordinates for whole-brain significant clusters in the provided full text. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical English MRI VBM study comparing heroin users vs controls), I5 (gray-matter measure: gray matter density), I6 (performed voxelwise whole-brain VBM comparisons yielding significant clusters). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (the full text as provided does not include reported peak coordinates x,y,z for any whole-brain significant cluster). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present) but lacks the required coordinate reporting needed for this meta-analysis, so the study cannot contribute coordinate foci and must be excluded on I7.

This is an empirical longitudinal MRI study (surface-based FreeSurfer analyses) comparing substance users (ALC, ALC+CU) to controls and reports a vertex-wise whole-hemisphere analysis with a significant cluster in right medial orbitofrontal cortex (p<.001). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (empirical MRI study), I5 (grey-matter surface-based measure — surface area), I6 (whole-brain vertex-wise analysis was performed), and I8 (voxel/vertex-wise results are reported in the manuscript text). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 — the paper, as provided, does not report peak coordinates (MNI/Talairach x,y,z) for the significant whole-brain/vertex-wise cluster(s). The meta-analysis requires reported peak coordinates for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered. Therefore exclude because I7 is not satisfied.

This study is excluded because it does not meet core inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Although it is an empirical MRI paper that performed VBM processing (so a gray-matter measure was computed) and reports participant demographics and MRI details, it does NOT report any whole-brain between-group voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts of gray-matter differences with significant peak coordinates. Specifically, it lacks (a) a reported whole-brain GM volume/density between-group result (I4 not met), (b) a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain contrast with reported coordinates (I6 not met), and (c) any significant GM foci/peak coordinates from such contrasts (I7 not met). In addition, the substance studied (betel quid/areca) is outside the five target pharmacological classes (alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis, stimulants) addressed by the meta-analysis, so the study does not address the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (the study computed gray-matter measures via VBM) and I9 (reports participant demographics, MRI field strength, preprocessing/software). Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: none of E5–E7. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) comparing opiate-dependent subjects to matched healthy controls, reporting gray-matter density differences (meets I4 and I5). The study performed whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (methods describe whole-brain spatial normalization and SPM99 t tests) and reports significant clusters (corrected p<0.01, t and extent thresholds) in prefrontal, insular, and temporal regions, with results referenced in Table 2 and figures (meets I6, I7, I8). Participant, substance-use, and MRI/method details are provided (meets I9). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; tables/figures are referenced in the text (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply (not an ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, non-empirical, or multivariate-classifier-only study). Therefore the study should be included.

Although this is an empirical English-language structural MRI study reporting subcortical grey-matter volumes and group comparisons, it does not report any voxelwise or vertexwise whole-brain between-group statistical maps with peak coordinates. The analysis used FIRST segmentation to extract regional (per-structure) volumes and performed region-wise/statistical tests (MANCOVA, post-hoc tests) rather than whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts. Therefore it fails the key whole-brain/coordinate-based inclusion criteria (I6 and I7) and must be excluded under exclusion criteria E5 (only ROI/region-based results) and E6 (per-region/parcellation analysis rather than voxelwise).

This study is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of prenatal alcohol exposure (ARDN) vs controls and reports vertex-wise (surface-based) whole-brain analyses with significant clusters in surface-area measures. It therefore meets I4 (empirical MRI study comparing groups), I5 (reports cortical thickness/volume/surface-based GM measures), I6 (performed vertexwise whole-brain contrasts), and I9 (reports participant age/sex, MRI field strength, and processing pipeline). However, the full text provided does not report any peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach) for the significant whole-brain clusters; I7 (reporting of at least one significant focus with peak coordinates) is not satisfied. Because I7 is required, the study cannot contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis and must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) are triggered by the article. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study of heroin (opioid) users vs. controls using voxelwise GM analyses (large genetic sample and an imaging VBM/DTI subset) and reports significant whole-brain cluster differences. Thus I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. The manuscript, as provided, describes voxelwise ANOVA results and refers to figures/tables for regional findings, so I8 is arguably satisfied. However, the provided full text does not include reported peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for the significant clusters, and I7 (requirement that whole-brain contrasts yield at least one significant cluster with reported peak coordinates) is not met based solely on the supplied content. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Because failure to meet I7 is sufficient for exclusion from the coordinate-based meta-analysis, the study must be excluded based on the information provided.

This study is an empirical English-language MRI study of alcoholics vs controls and reports regional grey-matter volume measures (I4, I5 satisfied). However, it does not report any voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain between-group statistical maps or peak coordinates: analyses are based on semi-automated/manual segmentation and region-of-interest (regional/parcellation) volume comparisons rather than a whole-brain voxelwise contrast. Therefore it fails I6 (whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast) and I7 (reported significant voxelwise foci with coordinates). It meets exclusion E5 (reports only ROI/parcellation results with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7. Exclusion criteria applied: E5.

This study is excluded because its between-group analyses are based on atlas-based parcellation (per-region average volumes using the SRI24 atlas) rather than voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical maps with reported peak coordinates. Thus it does not meet I6 (whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrast with coordinates) nor I7 (significant foci with reported coordinates). It is an empirical MRI study reporting gray-matter volume measures, so I4 and I5 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (results derived from predefined atlas parcellation / region averages) and E5 (ROI/parcellation-only analyses with no qualifying whole-brain voxelwise results). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5. Inclusion criteria not met: I6, I7.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between alcohol-dependent patients and controls (SPM5/VBM5; 1.5T). The paper reports whole-brain voxelwise two-sample t-tests (FDR-corrected) showing widespread significant GM reductions in alcoholics versus controls, and exploratory voxelwise regressions linking IGT performance to regional GM (with peaks plotted in MNI space and anatomical localization described). Although specific coordinate tables/figures are referenced rather than embedded in the provided text, the manuscript explicitly states peak coordinates were plotted and results are available in figures/tables, which satisfies the allowance for coordinates in tables/figures (I8). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study is an empirical structural MRI study comparing cocaine users and controls and uses cortical thickness measures (inclusion met: I4, I5). It reports MRI field strength and preprocessing software (I9). However, the imaging analysis is surface-based ROI/parcellation using the Desikan–Killiany atlas (mean thickness per region) rather than a voxelwise/vertexwise whole-brain statistical map, and no voxel/vertex coordinates or peak foci are reported. Therefore it does not provide qualifying whole-brain voxelwise/vertexwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates (inclusion I6 and I7 not met). This violates exclusion criteria E6 (results derived from atlas parcellation) and E5 (only ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain results). Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing heroin-dependent individuals to healthy controls using whole-brain surface-based morphometry (vertex-wise GLM across the cortex) and reports multiple significant clusters. The study uses a cortical grey-matter measure (cortical thickness), performs a vertexwise whole-brain analysis (with multiple-comparison correction), and indicates detailed cluster information (reported in tables/figures/supplement), which satisfies the requirement for significant whole-brain foci (reported peak information acceptable if in tables/supplement). Participant demographics, substance-use characteristics, field strength, and processing software are reported. The study also includes ROI analyses but crucially includes qualifying whole-brain vertexwise results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, atlas-only parcellation results only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8,I9) and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volume between current smokers (nicotine users) and never-smokers. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (SPM8/VBM8) with significant clusters surviving whole-brain FWE correction and provides MNI peak coordinates (Table 2 and Figure 1). It reports participant demographics, MRI field strength (1.5T), preprocessing and statistical software, and substance-use measures (pack-years). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas/parcellation-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports empirical English-language MRI results comparing substance-dependent individuals and controls and uses cortical thickness and cortical volume (FreeSurfer) (meets I4, I5). The authors performed whole-brain vertex-wise analyses (meets I6) but the whole-brain contrasts yielded no significant clusters after correction and no peak coordinates are reported; the paper’s reported significant findings are from atlas-based ROI/parcellation (Desikan-Killiany) analyses. Therefore it does NOT meet I7 (no significant whole-brain foci reported) and must be excluded per E5 (only ROI-significant results / no qualifying whole-brain results) and E6 (between-group results derived from predefined atlas parcellation rather than from significant voxelwise/vertexwise clusters). Full text appears complete. Inclusion met: I4, I5, I6. Inclusion not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E5, E6.

Article reports whole-brain vertexwise cortical thickness analyses (FreeSurfer QDEC) comparing adolescent substance use disorder patients and controls, finding a significant cluster (RACC-mOFC) with MNI coordinates. Cortical thickness is an accepted grey-matter measure for inclusion (I5). The study reports whole-brain voxel/vertexwise contrast with significant cluster and coordinates (I6,I7). Full text appears complete. It addresses substances broadly (patients had non-nicotine DSM-IV SUDs) relevant to meta-analysis objective across drug classes. Inclusion criteria I4-I9 satisfied.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing nicotine-dependent smokers to nonsmoking controls using voxel-based morphometry (GM volume) and reporting whole-cerebellum SUIT voxelwise results with significant clusters. The paper reports peak clusters (figures and Table 2 with MNI coordinates for Crus I), uses GM volume measures, and provides methodological details (participants’ age/sex, MRI field strength, preprocessing software). The SUIT cerebellum-restricted voxelwise map qualifies per the protocol (sub-volume voxelwise maps acceptable if coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, atlas-parcellation-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I4–I9) and should be included for coordinate-based meta-analysis of GM differences in substance users (nicotine).

Full text reports an empirical English-language structural MRI study comparing marijuana users and controls using grey-matter measures including cortical thickness and subcortical volumes (meets I4 and I5). The paper performed whole-brain vertexwise surface-based analyses (surface maps) and reports a significant cluster in the right fusiform gyrus (meets I6). No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it lacks reported peak coordinates for whole-brain significant foci required by the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical MRI VBM study comparing methamphetamine-exposed monkeys to saline controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise effects in the putamen, so it meets I4 (empirical MRI study of substance exposure vs controls), I5 (gray-matter measure via VBM), I6 (whole-brain voxelwise analysis was performed), I8 (results are reported in text/figures), and I9 (participant/scan details provided). However, the provided full text does not include peak coordinates (x,y,z) for the reported significant clusters; inclusion criterion I7 requires at least one whole-brain significant focus with reported MNI/Talairach coordinates. Because I7 is not satisfied in the provided full text, the study cannot be included. No exclusion criteria (E5–E7) apply based on the provided content.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using whole-brain voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volumes between cocaine-dependent individuals and non-drug-using controls. The manuscript is an empirical, English-language MRI study that assesses gray-matter volume differences between methamphetamine users and controls using voxel-based morphometry and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with significant clusters. Although this is an empirical English-language MRI study comparing methamphetamine users to controls and reports gray-matter measures (cortical volumes and thickness) and vertex-based whole-brain analyses with significant clusters, the full text as provided does not report peak coordinates (x,y,z in MNI or Talairach space) for any whole-brain significant clusters. This study examines chronic ketamine users (a dissociative anesthetic), which is not one of the five target pharmacological classes (alcohol, nicotine, opioids, cannabis, stimulants) required by the meta-analysis objective, so it does not address the review objective. This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare gray matter volume between adolescent cannabis users and matched controls. Although this is an empirical English-language MRI VBM study comparing MDMA (a stimulant) users to controls and reports whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and figures, the provided full text does not report numeric peak coordinates (x,y,z) for significant clusters. This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study comparing individuals with prenatal alcohol exposure (FASD) to matched controls using surface-based cortical thickness measures. This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter volumes between detoxified alcohol-dependent subjects and healthy controls. This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey-matter volume between chronic synthetic cannabinoid users and healthy controls. Methods report MRI field strength (3T), preprocessing and software (SPM8, SnPM), and participant demographics (male, ages reported). Thus it provides whole-brain voxelwise results with significant foci and sufficient methodological detail to contribute coordinates to the meta-analysis.
